mainTopic: Who can cancel the vows of a נערה המאורסה (an engaged young woman) when either her father or her husband dies before both have cancelled them
overview: A נערה המאורסה (an engaged young woman) has her vows cancelled only when her father and her husband both do הפרה together. This amud walks through what happens when one of them dies partway through. If the husband confirmed the vow, or heard it and stayed silent until the next day, the father cannot cancel it after the husband dies. If the father cancelled and then died, his power does not pass to the husband. If the husband cancelled and then died, the father takes over the full power and can cancel alone. If the husband cancelled and the father died, the husband cannot finish the cancellation by himself. The reason is that the husband can only cancel in partnership with the father.

steps.title: If the husband confirmed the vow before dying, the father cannot cancel it
steps.stepSummary: If the husband confirmed the vow, or heard it and stayed silent until the next day and then died, the father can no longer cancel the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the husband heard and confirmed the vow, or heard it, stayed silent, and died the next day, the father cannot cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The text gives the exception to an earlier rule: once the husband has confirmed the vow, the father cannot step in after the husband dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cancelling the vow of a נערה המאורסה needs both the father and the husband. If the husband confirmed it, his half of the partnership is gone forever. Staying silent for a whole day counts the same as confirming, so the vow stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: A young woman who is engaged (after אירוסין) but not yet fully married

steps.confusionAlert: The one who 'cannot cancel' here is the father, not the husband. The husband is already dead; the question is whether the father can still cancel the vow.

phrases.english: But if he heard and confirmed it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband of the engaged young woman.

phrases.english: or if he heard and was silent
and died on the following day,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the preceding rule (from before this text) that the father can cancel after the husband dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the husband has confirmed the vow, or stayed silent a full day, the father cannot cancel it after the husband's death.

steps.title: Father cancelled and then died: the husband does not take over
steps.stepSummary: If the father cancelled and died before the husband heard of the vow, this is the case behind the rule 'מת האב לא נתרוקנה רשות לבעל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her father heard and cancelled the vow, and the husband did not manage to hear about it before the father died, this is what we learned: if the father dies, the power does not pass over to the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The text explains a known rule ('if the father dies, the power does not pass to the husband') by showing the exact case it is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's cancellation alone is only half the job. When the father dies, the husband does not inherit the father's half. So the husband can never cancel this vow alone, and the vow stays.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not manage to (did not get the chance before something happened)
This is what we learned (this is the case behind a known teaching)
The authority was emptied over to someone else, so he gets full power

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the father's power and the husband's power are not equal. The husband's power depends on the father.

phrases.english: If her father heard and cancelled it for her,
and the husband did not manage to hear

phrases.aramaic: מֵת הָאָב, לֹא נִתְרוֹקְנָה רְשׁוּת לַבַּעַל.
phrases.english: If the father died, the authority does not pass over to the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the husband's death to the father's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the father cancelled and then died, the husband cannot complete the cancellation, because the father's power does not pass to him.

steps.title: Husband cancelled and then died: the father takes over
steps.stepSummary: If the husband cancelled and died before the father heard, this is the case behind the rule 'מת הבעל נתרוקנה רשות לאב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her husband heard and cancelled the vow, and the father did not manage to hear about it before the husband died, this is what we learned: if the husband dies, the power passes over to the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The text now explains the opposite rule, showing the case where the father gains full power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the last step, but with the opposite result. When the husband dies, the father gets full power over her vows, so he can cancel this vow by himself. The father is the main authority; the husband was only a partner.

phrases.english: If her husband heard and cancelled it for her,
and the father did not manage to hear
If the husband died, the authority passes over to the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁמַע בַּעְלָהּ וְהֵפֵר לָהּ וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק הָאָב לִשְׁמוֹעַ עַד שֶׁמֵּת הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror case of step 2, with the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the husband cancelled and then died, the father gets full authority and can cancel the vow alone.

steps.title: Husband cancelled and the father died: the husband cannot finish alone
steps.stepSummary: If the husband cancelled and the father died before hearing, the husband cannot cancel the vow, because he can only cancel together with the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her husband heard and cancelled the vow, and the father did not manage to hear about it before he died, the husband cannot cancel it, because the husband can only cancel in partnership.
steps.whatsHappening: The text gives a final case and states its reason: the husband's power only works as a partner with the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the husband is alive and the father died. Even though the husband already cancelled, his cancellation is worthless without the father's part. That is why, in step 2, the father's power did not pass to the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: In partnership, together with someone else

steps.whatToRemember: For a נערה המאורסה, the father is the main authority and the husband is only a partner. If the husband dies, the father takes full power. If the father dies, the husband cannot cancel alone.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Before he died' here means before the father died, not the husband. That is why the husband, who is still alive, is stuck.

phrases.english: If her husband heard and cancelled it for her,
and the father did not manage to hear

phrases.notes: 'He' is the father. The husband is still alive in this case.

phrases.english: because the husband cancels only in partnership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the case where the father dies after the husband has already cancelled. Its reason, that the husband cancels only in partnership, also explains step 2, where the father's power did not pass to the husband.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The husband's power over the vows of a נערה המאורסה only works together with the father. Without the father, the husband's cancellation does nothing.
